column230: I am looking for high-quality restaurants in this area. Unfortunately, we don't have any good options here, and whenever a new restaurant opens, it usually turns out to be mediocre. This region has a unique Key West vibe, and I believe we need an attractive anchor restaurant that can draw people from West Palm and Lake Park. We need a trendy restaurant with a well-designed interior and a menu catering to various customer segments. If I had the power, I would place an anchor restaurant on the water next to the Marina Grand, so that it has a public view of the water. I would also like to see a restaurant in the strip malls on Blue Heron or a proposed mixed-use development with indoor/outdoor seating or rooftop scenarios. An ideal option would be a restaurant with an enclosed patio at the back. Additionally, I would love to see a coffee shop, a yoga or Pilates studio, and a hip co-working space where I can rent a desk. I believe Riviera Beach needs to develop an industry plan that works well together and gives the city a sense of place. Currently, it feels like an industrial/logistics with a bedroom community jammed against it, there is no in-between. I would like to see more light industry or professional services filler such as law firms, financial services, etc. Lastly, I would love to see some live/work art studios along the working waterfront.
column285: The City seems to focus its energy on tackling big lot redevelopment but fails to do much, if anything, with the surrounding neighborhoods. I often hear people who live in HOAs comment that services are okay with the City, but I think that's because many of those "services" are covered by the HOA. The downtown corridor needs to be re-imagined as a walkable, engaging community, as opposed to a series of one-off shiny redevelopments surrounded by blight; more must be done by the CRA to make the downtown area's neighborhoods vibrant, continuous, and visitor and resident-friendly.

column230: What I would like to see Riviera Beach bring to the city is more life to the city. Right now, all you see is new high rises that most who are true residents in Riviera Beach cannot afford. Instead of flushing certain people out make it where all can benefit in the city. Many individuals living here grew up here and are very excited for change. We need to recognize the youth more in the newsletter no matter what school they went to. If they reside in Riviera Beach, let's bring some light to these young girls and boys. We have a lot of talented kids in the city. We need to bring more awareness to homeownership, credit and more. I would love to assist with this as that is what my company does. So many people want to purchase homes but don't know where to start. Let's bring more awareness and utilize those in the community to help put these together. Also, for those who play sports let's try to set up an event that brings the scouts to our talent so we can have more individuals getting college scholarships and going further with their dreams. The change is here. We may be a small city, but we got to have BIG thought when it comes to uplifting this city and getting more involved.  Please contact me as I would love to assist with this.

Yhis survey had no questions about the water services. I have to believe that is due to the terrible  known quality of the yellowish water we are service. We just found out last summer that the water lines in Singer Island had never been flushed, holding lots of sediment. The longterm planning and maintance has been an issue. We pay alot in taxes and water bills... Many of us expect better, and to not have the water service included within this survey seems to show a lack of transparency for all feedback from the residents of Riviera Beach. This makes me wonder what else is missing.
Also it was not asked how we thought about outsourcing other services such as lawn care. I would.like to understand if insourcing and the cost of retirements is the best for all tax payers of Riviera Beach.
